## BLUF

Both features shipped to `master`, CI green for each, drop ready for the Windows box.

1. **Triple-click** (`<leader>t`): `ClickAction.Triple` + `DoTripleClick` (three bare
   `mouse_event` pairs, no sleep). Commit `3fa79c9`; CI `31711412235` (52s).
2. **Text-span selection** (`<leader>v`): a 2-pick sub-phase mirroring `<leader>s` snapshot;
   type the start label, then the end label → the text between is selected. Gesture is the
   new hot-reload `TextSelectMethod` key (`ShiftClick` default | `Drag`). Commit `9f750df`;
   CI `31712258308` (1m4s).

Plan: [`20260813-223634_triple-click-and-text-select.plan.qmd`](20260813-223634_triple-click-and-text-select.plan.qmd).

## Key design decision (resolved mid-impl)

The gesture fork (Shift-click vs Drag) was left open by the user, so **both ship behind one
hot-reload key** and the Windows box picks the winner — input synthesis cannot be tested on
Linux. Default `ShiftClick`.

**Refinement over the plan:** the original Drag design held the mouse button across the
second-pick typing, which could leave the button stuck on a non-Esc close (auto-close / a
dismiss path that bypasses `HandleEscape`) — a silent-failure the project rules forbid.
Replaced with an **atomic one-shot drag at pick-2**: pick-1 only remembers the start point; pick-2
does `SetCursorPos(anchor); LEFTDOWN; SetCursorPos(end); LEFTUP`. No button is ever held between
picks, so no cancel/close path can leave it stuck. ShiftClick was always clean (plain click +
Shift+click, two complete click cycles).

## Verification

- **CI** (`.github/workflows/build.yml`, windows-latest, MSBuild + vstest) — **GREEN** for
  both: `31711412235` (triple, 52s) and `31712258308` (select, 1m4s); Build + Test + Upload ✓.
  Only annotation is the pre-existing Node.js 20 deprecation (unrelated).
- **Prereq (Shift synthesis vs. our own hook):** verified by reading
  `OverlayKeyboardHook.cs:240-274` — the LL keyboard hook has no injected-swallow and only
  gates on Alt/Capslock-held/suspended; `VK_SHIFT` is not a captured key (`Classify`→`None`→
  pass-through), and the action runs on the UI thread via `_dispatcher.BeginInvoke` (`:311`),
  not inside the hook callback. So the synthesized Shift reaches the app's key state. **No
  hook change was needed.**
- **Unit tests:** new — `ParseTextSelectMethod` (known values + fallback), `t=Triple`,
  `v=SelectText` (+ `Select` alias); existing leader-default/display-label tests updated to
  the 11-binding default. The select phase machine and click synthesis are NOT unit-tested
  (need a live cursor/input system — same bar as `Double` and snapshot's `HandleSnapshotCorner`).
- **Manual (Windows box):** the only gate CI cannot cover. Triple-click selects a line;
  `<leader>v` + two labels selects the span (ShiftClick); flip `TextSelectMethod=Drag`
  (hot-reload) → drag selects. **Quit the old `hap.exe` (tray → Exit) before launching.**

## Risks / follow-ups

- **Triple-click timing** — no-sleep should register (double-click does, and the click is off
  the LL-hook thread); on-box verify. If an app misses the middle click, a tiny inter-click
  delay is the fix (eats the 300ms LL-hook budget, so no-sleep is preferred).
- **Shift+click remapped by some apps** (column-select) — the reason `Drag` ships as the
  fallback; flip via `TextSelectMethod`.
- **Synthesized drag as a click** — if start/end are within the drag threshold (~4px) the OS
  may see a click, not a drag. Acceptable (two distinct labels are usually far apart).
- On-box visual/behavioral check is the final gate for both features.
